name: Gamaliel
overview: Gamaliel was a male Pharisee and a respected member of the Jewish Council, also known as the Sanhedrin. His role in the early church is highlighted by his position within this authoritative body, where he was known for his wisdom and moderation. No additional personal notes or tribal affiliations are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Gamaliel means 'recompense of God [El],' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in Hebrew. This proper name, as recorded, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful reference to divine recompense.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Gamaliel beyond his identification as a Pharisee and council member. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text concerning his lineage or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Gamaliel's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his influential role as a Pharisee and member of the Jewish Council during the early days of the Christian church. His presence in the council suggests he was a figure of authority and wisdom, contributing to decisions that affected the early followers of Christ. His counsel is noted for its moderation and respect for divine providence, marking him as a key figure in the unfolding of the New Testament events.
